defects.title: Evidence-bound certificate issuance
defects.red_observation: arbitrary caller-created CertificateStore + issue() authorized formal eligibility with empty evidence_ref, empty reference identity, and reference == production; certificates carried zero digest bindings
defects.repair: QualificationAuthority is the only trusted issuance path: verifies mandatory gate evidence (all implementation files exist + non-empty, actual sha256 digests computed from bytes, reference oracle must differ from production evaluator, evidence files required); certificates bind 8 implementation digests + replay contract + protocol + evidence refs + limitations; arbitrary stores are untrusted and never authorize; validate_certificate rejects incomplete/incompatible certificates; registries carry a self-checksum
defects.trust_boundary: in-process Python cannot defend against a malicious caller that forges the trusted=True flag or monkeypatches the authority; the enforced boundary is against ACCIDENTAL misuse and untrusted data. No cryptographic signatures, no remote enforcement (not implemented, not claimed). Full lifecycle (signed receipts, scope hierarchies) is EA17.

defects.title: Verified evidence must establish actual provenance
defects.red_observation: 'banana' accepted as SHA256; 63-char digest accepted; identical untrusted digest pair accepted with basis 'no bytes were ever read'; VerifiedEvidence directly constructible; envelope identity dict mutable ('hacked')
defects.repair: strict 64-hex digest syntax (validate_sha256_digest); VerifiedEvidence + VerificationReceipt require a private creation key (direct construction raises PermissionError); identity/verification_checks exposed as read-only mappings over defensive copies; VerificationReceipts hash the artifact's actual bytes and bind trial+experiment identity (mismatch fails closed); the N02RR adapter now consumes receipts instead of caller-supplied digest strings; three evidence classes documented (claimed / actually-verified / qualified transfer)

defects.title: Formal publication boundary hardening
defects.red_observation: empty, unrelated and revoked-only certificate stores all produced ALLOWED; zero qualified rows produced ALLOWED; critical NOT_EVALUABLE rows did not block; no roster, no duplicate detection, no scope enforcement
defects.repair: publication requires a trusted store with a currently-valid certificate FOR THE REQUESTED SCOPE (BLOCKED_SCOPE_NOT_CERTIFIED otherwise); zero qualified rows blocked; critical NOT_EVALUABLE (error pipeline / rejected evidence / evidence-invalid markers) blocks the scope; duplicate trial identities quarantined; planned-roster reconciliation reports every slot with missing slots blocking unless an explicit partial scope is declared (scope_declaration='partial', never full closure); conditional accuracy and evaluation coverage reported separately
defects.regression: test_wavebc_hardening.TestEAR03PublicationBoundary (4 tests) + test_boundary rework (EA00 regression phases updated: contaminated scope now BLOCKED_CRITICAL_NOT_EVALUABLE; sealed-only scope ALLOWED with exact roster; partial scope explicit)

defects.title: Qualification revocation and time-of-check integrity
defects.red_observation: aggregation report survived post-aggregation revocation (ALLOWED persisted); records mutable after validation; reissuing an equivalent certificate was immediately valid; corrupted registry crashed with an uncontrolled JSONDecodeError
defects.repair: immutable checksummed QualificationSnapshot; publish_report rechecks snapshot currency AND per-certificate validity at publication time (revocation between aggregation and publication raises and downgrades the report); durable revocation history persisted atomically (temp + os.replace) with registry self-checksum (corrupt/tampered registries fail closed with CertificateError); reissuing a revoked binding requires requalified=True with fresh gate evidence; store mutations synchronized under an RLock
defects.residual: EvaluationResult remains a mutable dataclass by design (records are working objects); the boundary re-validates every record at aggregation and binds publication to the snapshot, which is the enforced time-of-check seam. Concurrency tests use threads where applicable; multi-process mutual exclusion is documented as EA17 scope.

note: These four repairs are hardening WITHIN EA05-EA08/EA10-EA11 scopes per the addendum; they do not by themselves grant any Wave B gate. Wave B proper (EA03-EA08 independent semantic qualification) proceeds on top of this trusted boundary.
